correctness.rationale: Every length-b substitution block contains exactly one 1; the exact prefix formula F(bp+s)=p+[s>0]x_p gives the stated factor-weight equation at arbitrary starting phases. Aperiodicity is established by residue-zero versus forced-zero interior positions and by contraction of any eventual period divisible by b. A bounded telescoping sum then forces both 0->1 and 1->0 at each positive separation. Enumerating all start-phase cases proves exact extrema for each remainder. Unit-size changes of weights under shifting the factor make all integers between these extrema appear. Independent code compares both recurrence and exhaustive finite factor spectra for 2<=b<=17.

value.rationale: The 2024 source asks whether Parikh-constant morphisms have ultimately periodic Abelian complexity. For a canonical binary parameter family extending the Thue-Morse substitution, the theorem answers that question affirmatively in the family, computes not only cardinalities but every Parikh vector at every length, and exhibits a sharp change in balance constant at b=4. The parameter b is structural, and the b-periodic support is a genuine all-parameter theorem rather than a finite slice or an unmotivated invariant.
